note_sections.t: Re-evaluation for treatment decision following rapid PSA rise and prior biopsy-proven Gleason 4+3 prostate cancer.

Recently retired logistics manager with a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. The patient was diagnosed with prostate cancer earlier this year following an elevated PSA, with biopsy confirming Gleason 4+3 disease. Since then, PSA levels have risen sharply from 1.2 ng/mL in December 2023 to 9.3 ng/mL in January 2025. He reports moderate lower urinary tract symptoms with an IPSS score of 16/35. Socially, he is married, lives with his partner, and has adult children who visit weekly. He consumes approximately 24 units of alcohol per week and maintains a sedentary lifestyle with occasional walking. Recent appointments include a pulmonary function test for known COPD, quarterly diabetes nurse reviews, and a stable annual cardiology review in autumn 2024.

On DRE, a suspicious nodule is palpable in the right peripheral zone of the prostate, consistent with clinical stage cT1c. The prostate is small, measuring approximately 18 mL. General examination reveals a well-nourished man with stable vital signs, blood pressure 139/63 mmHg, and heart rate 72 bpm.
